conversation.text:
## Summary

Based on my assessment of your situation against the official UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, here's the outcome:

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for 1 out of 3 children:**

### ✅ **Charlie (Age 11) - ELIGIBLE**
Charlie lives with you and meets all the criteria for Child Benefit. As Charlie is under 16, lives with you, and is not in care, hospital, or working 24+ hours/week, you qualify for Child Benefit for Charlie.

### ❌ **Alex (Age 21) - INELIGIBLE**
Alex is too old for Child Benefit. The maximum age is under 20 (and only if in approved education or training). Additionally, Alex works 24+ hours per week and is not in approved education, which would disqualify them even if under 20.

### ❌ **Blake (Age 15) - INELIGIBLE**
While Blake is the right age (under 16), Blake doesn't live with you, and your contribution of £10/week is insufficient. To continue receiving Child Benefit for a child who lives elsewhere beyond the initial 8 weeks, you must contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (approximately £16.95-£25.60/week depending on whether they're the eldest or additional child). Your £10/week contribution falls short of this requirement.

**What you can do:** You should apply for Child Benefit for Charlie. If you increase your contributions to Blake to at least the Child Benefit amount, you could potentially become eligible for Blake as well.

reasonings: Alex is 21 years old. According to the eligibility rules, Child Benefit is available for children under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Alex works 24+ hours per week and is not in approved education. The rules clearly state: 'You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.' Although you contribute £50/week towards Alex's upkeep and Alex doesn't live with you, Alex is over 20 years old and working full-time, which means you are ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Blake is 15 years old (under 16), so meets the age requirement. Blake does not live with you, but you contribute £10/week towards Blake's upkeep. According to the rules for children who live with someone else, you could continue to get payments for more than 8 weeks if you 'contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.' The current Child Benefit rate is approximately £25.60/week for the eldest child and £16.95/week for additional children. Your contribution of £10/week is less than the Child Benefit amount, so you do not meet the threshold to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks. You are therefore ineligible for Child Benefit for Blake.

Charlie is 11 years old (under 16) and lives with you. You are responsible for Charlie as you live together. Charlie is not in local authority care, not fostered, not in hospital or residential accommodation, does not work 24+ hours per week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right. Charlie meets all the eligibility criteria, and you are eligible for Child Benefit for Charlie.
